final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and instead reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is useful, but it is not enough to reach compliant_with_caveats here. The policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. Admissible evidence still shows the field-service dispatch segment is below target and remains exposed, while the only risk-acceptance record is unapproved and does not cover that exposure. The Actor also concedes there is no evidence that the required disclosure artifact has already been prepared or approved. That means the caveat is not merely explanatory; it is an unmet compliance condition. The admissible record supports that caveated certification could become supportable if launch-time disclosure is actually in place, but it does not support concluding that condition has been met now.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the required launch-time model-card disclosure for the field-service dispatch limitation has been prepared, reviewed, or approved.
The affected field-service dispatch segment remains exposed in the initial 6% rollout cohort, so rollout controls and monitoring do not satisfy the policy on their own.
The only risk-acceptance artifact is an unapproved draft with a blank approver line and it does not address field-service dispatch exposure.

The Actor's narrower framing is more accurate than an unqualified certification theory, but it still depends on an unresolved compliance predicate: actual launch disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
